q: How much fuel can a Bikaner POP furnace save by preheating combustion air from its flue gas?
title: Bikaner POP furnace: air preheat saving
short: Roughly a tenth of the petcoke. Flue gas leaves Bikaner's plaster of Paris furnaces at 700 to 800 C and could heat combustion air to 250 to 300 C. TERI's rule: every 20 C of air preheat saves 1% of fuel, and it puts the cluster's saving potential at 10 to 15%.
audience: Plaster of Paris makers in Khara and other RIICO industrial areas of Bikaner, Rajasthan

sections.h: Why the chimney is where the money goes
ul: Gypsum in the drum only needs about 150 to 200 C to turn into plaster of Paris; the furnace is run at around 1,000 C.
The flue gas leaves through a small chimney above 700 C, and nothing recovers it.
Walls are clay brick with no insulation, the drum has no fins, and firing is judged by eye.
Petcoke feed is held constant while air is changed by hand, so unburnt coke clogs the burner orifices and shows as black smoke.

p: Every 22 C drop in flue gas temperature, or every 20 C rise in combustion air temperature, saves about 1% of fuel. They describe the same heat, so count one, not both. Air heated from about 35 C to 250 C is a rise of 215 C, about 10.7%.

ul: Temperature probes at the crown in at least three places, and on the drum, so firing is not done by eye.
Coke feed matched to airflow and furnace temperature, so less coke falls unburnt.
Insulating brick and ceramic fibre in walls, floor and crown.
Fins on the drum to pass more heat to the gypsum.
A redesigned furnace with all of these and the recuperator: about 20% less energy, in TERI's estimate.

p: Bikaner units burn 50 to 60 kg of petcoke per tonne of gypsum charged. Weigh coke per batch and POP bagged for a month before the change and a month after; that kilogram per tonne is the figure a lender will look for.

example.title: A three shift unit making 6,000 t a year (estimate)
lines: Petcoke: 330 t a year, 55 kg per tonne of POP
10% saved by air preheat: 33 t of coke
At Rs 10,000 per tonne, the profile's 2016 price: Rs 3.3 lakh a year
CO2 at the IPCC petcoke default, about 3.17 t per tonne: 33 t x 3.17 = about 105 t a year
Whole unit: 330 t x 3.17 = 1,046 t + 175,000 kWh x 0.675 = 118 t; about 194 kg CO2 per tonne of POP
example.note: Temperatures, rules of thumb, coke use and unit sizes from TERI's Bikaner plaster of Paris cluster profile (2016). The 35 C starting air temperature is an assumption. Petcoke CO2 is our estimate from the IPCC 2006 default (97.5 kg per GJ at 32.5 GJ per tonne); grid factor CEA FY 2025-26.
